headlines.title: Vallejo father and teen son speak out after surviving Fairfield Spirit Halloween mass shooting
headlines.description: A Vallejo man says he and his teenage son will never be the same after both were shot during last month’s mass shooting at a Spirit Halloween store in Fairfield. Now that both have finally returned home from the hospital, Anthony Barlow Jr. is speaking out about the terrifying ordeal on Oct. 30, when a 17-year-old suspect opened fire inside the store the night before Halloween. “Wasn’t no warning, there wasn’t no arguments. We didn’t hear nothing to give us a heads up about what was about to happen,” Barlow said. “All I heard was shots — real loud shots.” Barlow said he never saw the attack coming. Earlier that evening, he and his children had just finished carving pumpkins and eating pizza when his 16-year-old son, Anthony Barlow III, asked for a ride to the store to get a different costume. Barlow had just finished paying for their items when gunfire erupted. “I knew I was bleeding. I knew I was hit, but I couldn’t tell how bad it was,” he said. “I just felt the pain.” While Barlow realized he had been wounded, he did not initially know his son had also been shot. The father and son were separated in the chaos as screaming shoppers stampeded toward the exits to escape. Barlow was transported to Kaiser Permanente in Vallejo, while his son was rushed to a separate hospital. “They took him to NorthBay right across the street, and that’s pretty much what saved his life, is him going to NorthBay,” Barlow said. A bullet shattered Barlow’s elbow, while his son suffered more severe injuries, including a collapsed lung. The two did not reunite until 10 days after the shooting. “Physically just being able to touch him and hold him and kiss him and tell him how much I love him,” Barlow said of seeing his son again. Anthony Barlow III was released from the hospital on Friday. A GoFundMe campaign has been organized to help the father of nine and his son recover and get back on their feet. “This has impacted our life forever, and every Halloween that come up from here on out, we’re gonna remember that day, Oct. 30,” Barlow said. “We have a lot to be thankful for this year — thankful for our lives, thankful for all the prayers, the family, all the love and support we’ve been getting. We’re just thankful for it all.”
